evidence: Repo-wide grep for pendingOwner: the ONLY writes are InsightsDashboardViewModel.kt:147,153,158 — which write to the injected InsightsNavRelay (a different @Singleton in the insights package), plus tests. BookingPageOwnerRelay.pendingOwner's sole assignment is its own consume() clearing it to null (BookingPageOwnerRelay.kt:29), despite its KDoc claiming 'The navigation graph (RootTabScreen) sets [pendingOwner] before navigating'. RootTabScreen.kt:2446/2452 register BOOKING_PAGE_MANAGE / PUBLIC_PAGE_PREVIEW as arg-less composables that set nothing. Both consumers hard-fall-back: BookingPageManageViewModel injects BookingPageOwnerRelay and does `private val owner = ownerRelay.consume() ?: SchedulingOwner.Personal`; PublicPagePreviewViewModel has the identical line. Every navigation entry uses the bare constant with no owner: InsightsDashboardViewModel.bookingPageRoute() (line 162, sets NO relay — contrast its openTypeRoute/openNoShowRoute/openTeamRoute which do set InsightsNavRelay.pendingOwner), EventTypePerformanceViewModel.kt:171 bookingPageRoute(), BookingsInboxViewModel.kt:136 shareRoute(), GroupRosterViewModel.kt:194 onShareLink. So the booking-page manage/preview screens are permanently Personal: a business owner reaching them from business insights loads and SAVES against the personal page (updateSlug/updateBookingPage with Personal), overwriting personal content and leaving the business page unreachable on Android.

Parameterise BookingPageManageViewModelTest assertions that currently pin Personal.

evidence: SlotPickerViewModel.kt loadSlots() (working tree, ~line 187-189): `val from = maxOf(month.atDay(1), LocalDate.now(zone())).toString(); val to = month.atEndOfMonth().toString()` — date-only strings sent to GET /book/:slug/:eventTypeSlug/slots. Route (backend/routes/schedulingPublic.js:156-179, current tree) forwards from/to verbatim into availabilityService.computeSlots with no end-of-day adjustment. computeSlots (availabilityService.js:485-492): `const toMs = Math.min(new Date(to).getTime(), horizonMs)` — ECMA-262 parses a date-only string as UTC midnight, so to='2026-06-30' gives toMs=2026-06-30T00:00:00Z. computeSlotsCore line 300: `if (s < effectiveFrom || s > effectiveTo || e > toMs) continue;` — no slot may END after the last day's UTC midnight. Hence for viewers at or west of UTC the entire last calendar day of every month yields zero slots (and slots late on the second-to-last local day are also cut, e.g. after 17:00 PDT); east of UTC only slots ending before offset-hours local time survive. The month grid derives tappable days from returned slots (availableDaysIn(visibleMonth, slots) in fetchMonth/emitContent), so the last day renders permanently unavailable, and seeNextAvailable()'s month scan repeats the truncation each month.
fix: Send an exclusive end: `val to = month.atEndOfMonth().plusDays(1).toString()` (or a full instant `month.atEndOfMonth().plusDays(1).atStartOfDay(zone()).toInstant().toString()`), covering the whole last local day. Applies to both the slug path and the one-off-token path in loadSlots().

evidence: PackageEditorViewModel.kt (working tree) seed() line 298: `priceText = pkg.priceCents.takeIf { it > 0 }?.let { "%.2f".format(it / CENTS_PER_UNIT) } ?: ""` with `CENTS_PER_UNIT = 100.0` (line 321). Kotlin's `"%.2f".format(x)` is java.lang.String.format with NO locale argument, i.e. Locale.getDefault(Locale.Category.FORMAT): on any comma-decimal locale (de-DE, fr-FR, ...) 22000 cents seeds the field as "220,00". save() line 222: `val priceCents = PackagesMoney.parseCents(form.priceText) ?: 0` sent unconditionally in Update/CreatePackageRequest (lines 232/244). PackagesKit.kt parseCents (lines 121-126): `raw.filter { it.isDigit() || it == '.' }` — ASCII '.' only, the comma is silently DROPPED (not treated as a separator) -> "22000" -> toDoubleOrNull()=22000.0 -> *100.0 -> roundToInt = 2,200,000 cents. So opening a EUR-locale editor on a $220.00 package and saving any unrelated edit PUTs price_cents=2200000 ($22,000.00) — exact 100x inflation. Fresh typed input "240,50" via the KeyboardType.Decimal field (PackageEditorScreen.kt:243) corrupts identically. Formatter locale: default FORMAT category; parser locale: none (hand-rolled ASCII digit+dot filter).
fix: Pin both sides: `String.format(Locale.US, "%.2f", pkg.priceCents / 100.0)` in seed(), and normalize in parseCents (strip grouping, accept ',' as decimal: e.g. filter digits+'.'+',' then replace(',', '.') keeping only the last separator). Add a comma-decimal-locale unit test (existing test only asserts "220.00" under the JVM default).

evidence: Current tree: OnboardingHomeBusinessViewModel.eventTypeRequest() business branch (lines ~355-365) sets `priceCents = s.priceText.toIntOrNull()?.times(CENTS_PER_DOLLAR)` UNCONDITIONALLY, with priceText defaulting to "120" (state line 55) and the price field always rendered in BusinessStep (OnboardingHomeBusinessScreen.kt:158-162). The VM's constructor injects only repo/homes/auth/errors — SchedulingFeatureFlags is not referenced anywhere in the file. iOS gates exactly this: SchedulingOnboardingModel.swift:329 `let priceCents: Int? = (flow == .business && paidEnabled) ? (Int(priceText).map { $0 * 100 }) : nil`. The flags also diverge as claimed: Android SchedulingFeatureFlags.paidSchedulingEnabled = `environment != ENV_PRODUCTION` (SchedulingFeatureFlags.kt:28-29, BuildConfig.PANTOPUS_ENV-driven), iOS paidEnabled is a UserDefaults bool defaulting false (SchedulingFeatureFlags.swift:25-33). So a default business onboarding run on Android creates price_cents=12000 — including in production builds where the client's paid-scheduling UI is explicitly disabled — while the identical iOS run creates a free service. evidence: InvoiceDto (InvoiceDtos.kt, working tree) models exactly id/business_user_id/recipient_user_id/total_cents/currency/line_items/created_at — no status, paid_at, due_date, subtotal_cents or fee_cents. Backend returns the whole row: scheduling.js:1214 (list) and :1218 (detail) `.from('BusinessInvoice').select('*')`, and supabase/migrations/20260315000015_business_invoice.sql defines status (line 12, with CHECK constraint), due_date (13), paid_at (16), subtotal_cents (8), fee_cents (9). Moshi generateAdapter silently drops the unmodelled keys. InvoicesListViewModel.load() then computes `outstandingLabel = PackagesMoney.format(invoices.sumOf { it.totalCents ?: 0 })` over EVERY invoice, `collectedMonthLabel = format(0)`, `hasOverdue = false` — with in-code comments admitting all three ('cannot compute the real outstanding vs collected split', 'Deferred: always false until DTO has status'). evidence: SchedulingPublicApi.kt:103-107: `@Streaming @GET("api/public/booking/{token}/ics") suspend fun getIcs(...): ResponseBody` — with @Streaming Retrofit hands over the raw UNREAD body. SchedulingRepository.kt:621: `publicGetIcs(token) = safeApiCall { publicApi.getIcs(token) }` — and SafeApiCall.kt:19-38 is a bare try/catch with no dispatcher hop, so the unconsumed body propagates. Sole caller AddToCalendarViewModel.downloadIcs(): `viewModelScope.launch { ... runCatching { result.data.string() } ... }` — viewModelScope is Dispatchers.Main.immediate, so ResponseBody.string() performs the blocking socket read on the MAIN thread. Concretely on-device: if the remaining bytes require a socket read, Android's default thread policy raises NetworkOnMainThreadException, which the runCatching swallows into 'Couldn't prepare the calendar file.' — i.e. the feature errors (or, when bytes happen to be pre-buffered, silently blocks main); on a stalled read it is an ANR. Close/leak half also verified: nothing closes the body if the coroutine is cancelled between Success and .string() (string() itself is the only closer), leaking the connection.
fix: Consume in the repository off-main and return decoded text: `publicGetIcs(token): NetworkResult<String> = safeApiCall { withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { publicApi.getIcs(token).use { it.string() } } }`; AddToCalendarViewModel then uses result.data directly.

evidence: AvailabilityFormat.kt: `fun hhmm(hour, minute): String = "%02d:%02d".format(hour, minute)` — kotlin.text String.format extension = java.lang.String.format with Locale.getDefault(Locale.Category.FORMAT); on Android, Formatter substitutes the locale zero digit, so ar-EG/fa-IR devices produce Arabic-Indic digits. This IS the wire format, not display: quarterHourOptions() (AvailabilityPickers.kt:55-61) builds each picker VALUE as hhmm(hour, minute); TimeRangeEditorSheet holds `start = normalizeHHmm(initialStart)` where normalizeHHmm() re-derives even server-loaded times through hhmm(); onConfirm hands the strings to updateBlock, and WeeklyHoursEditorViewModel.save() flat-maps them into `RuleInput(day.weekday, it.start, it.end)` for PUT rules. Backend rulesSchema (scheduling.js:565-571): `start_time: Joi.string().pattern(/^\d{2}:\d{2}(:\d{2})?$/)` — JS \d is ASCII-only, so the request 400s and finishSaveWithError shows a generic error. formatTime12 (same file) shares the unpinned format (display-only). Failure path traces: Arabic-locale device can never save weekly hours; invisible on en-US devices/JVM CI.
fix: Pin the wire formatter: String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%02d:%02d", hour, minute) in hhmm (and Locale.US in formatTime12 for display consistency); add an ar-EG Locale.setDefault round-trip unit test.

evidence: WeeklyHoursEditorViewModel.updateBlock (lines 210-221) stores TimeRange(start, end) verbatim with no ordering check, and save() (~255-263) flat-maps every enabled day's blocks into RuleInput with no validation. TimeRangeEditorSheet (AvailabilityPickers.kt:75-116) offers two independent 24h columns and its `A3PrimaryButton(label = "Set ...", onClick = { onConfirm(start, end) })` is never disabled. WeeklyHoursEditorScreen.kt:159 calls `A3SaveBar(label, saving, onSave)` omitting the `enabled` parameter, whose default is true (AvailabilityComponents.kt:665-670). Backend does not defend: rulesSchema (scheduling.js:565-571) is pattern-only, and buildWeeklyWindows (availabilityService.js:194-202) silently drops the window via `if (endMs > startMs) windows.push(...)` — so an inverted range saves 200 OK and zeroes that day's public availability with no error anywhere. DateOverridesViewModel.applySelected (lines 176-185) writes customStart/customEnd with the identical gap. iOS guards both: WeeklyHoursEditorViewModel.swift:80-83 formValid rejects any !range.isValid and save() guards on it (line 279).
fix: Add a minutes-since-midnight isValid to TimeRange, derive WeeklyHoursForm.isValid (every enabled day has >=1 block, none inverted), early-return in save() and pass enabled=form.isValid to A3SaveBar; mirror in DateOverridesViewModel.applySelected; optionally disable the sheet confirm when start >= end.

evidence: BookingLimitsViewModel.kt (working tree): toForm() (lines 123-133) is lossy — `minNoticeHours = (minNoticeMin ?: DEFAULT_NOTICE_MIN) / MIN_PER_HOUR` (DEFAULT_NOTICE_MIN=240, MIN_PER_HOUR=60; integer division turns a 30-min notice into 0h), `maxPerDay = (dailyCap ?: DEFAULT_DAILY_CAP).coerceAtLeast(MIN_CAP)` / same for perPerson (null cap = 'no limit' per migration 159_calendarly_core.sql lines 186-187 nullable integers, collapsed to a concrete default), and `startInterval = StartInterval.fromMinutes(slotIntervalMin)` where fromMinutes maps anything != 60/30 to Quarter=15 (AvailabilityFormat.kt:274-280) though backend permits 5..240. save() (lines 157-166) then builds UpdateEventTypeRequest with ALL FIVE fields unconditionally — no dirty tracking, and `dailyCap = form.maxPerDay.takeIf { it > 0 }` is always non-null since the form clamps to MIN_CAP >= 1. Backend PUT is a true partial patch (eventTypePatchSchema, scheduling.js:338-372: every key optional, daily_cap/per_booker_cap `.allow(null)`), so sending fewer fields is fully supported. iOS documents and implements exactly the per-field-dirty behavior (BookingLimits/BookingLimitsViewModel.swift:12-18 comment + loaded-value snapshots). Failure path traces: open Booking limits on an unlimited event type, bump only the horizon, save — daily_cap gets written to the form default and the 9th booker of a day is refused; a web-configured 30-min notice becomes 0.
fix: Snapshot loaded DTO values in toForm and include a field in UpdateEventTypeRequest only when the control moved off its loaded value (Moshi omits nulls); keep nullable loadedDailyCap/loadedPerBookerCap so untouched null stays null. Rewrite BookingLimitsViewModelTest's full-body assertion which currently certifies the defect.

evidence: EventTypeListScreen.kt: FilterHeader declares `@Suppress("UNUSED_PARAMETER") onSelectPillar: (SchedulingPillar) -> Unit` and renders only a static PillarIdentityPill (comment: 'The switcher row is NOT in the design — the user arrives scoped to one owner') — yet nothing scopes the arrival. The screen passes viewModel::selectPillar (line 153) but it is never invoked, so EventTypeListViewModel._pillar/owner stay at their initial SchedulingPillar.Personal / `private var owner: SchedulingOwner = SchedulingOwner.Personal`; selectPillar/resolveOwner/noOwnerMessage are dead code, and start() consumes no relay. Nothing supplies the owner externally: SchedulingRoutes.EVENT_TYPE_LIST is an arg-less constant registered bare at RootTabScreen.kt:2378, the hub navigates with the bare constant (SchedulingHubViewModel.kt:389, current tree — parallel design fixes did not touch this), and SchedulingEditorOwnerRelay.pending is written only inside the eventtypes package (EventTypeListViewModel.kt:335/340 createRoute/editorRoute, EventTypeEditorViewModel.kt:269) — the BookingsInbox write at BookingsInboxViewModel.kt:140 targets the separate BookingsOwnerRelay class. The VM's own doc ('the pillar pill re-scopes via HomesRepository/AuthRepository') describes behavior that does not exist. Failure path traces: Business hub -> Event types opens the Personal catalog; '+' -> createRoute() sets relay.pending = Personal, so the new service is created with no owner fields and lands on the personal booking page; Home users can never manage household services here.
fix: Either wire the pill row to onSelectPillar (drop the @Suppress), or preferably carry the hub's resolved owner: hub sets SchedulingEditorOwnerRelay.pending = owner (or a route arg via the new SchedulingOwner.routeKind machinery) before navigating, and EventTypeListViewModel.start() consumes it as the initial owner/pillar.

evidence: EventTypeEditorScreen.kt:440: `value = (form.priceCents / 100).toString()` — integer division, so a $49.99 service (price_cents=4999) renders as "49" and the cents are invisible. EventTypeEditorViewModel.onPrice (lines 186-192): `val cents = dollars.filter { c -> c.isDigit() }.toIntOrNull()?.times(100) ?: 0` — the decimal separator is STRIPPED, not interpreted: "49.99" -> digit-string "4999" -> 499,900 cents ($4,999.00, a 100x inflation); it also cascades into depositCents (= cents/2 when deposit mode on). Even without decimals, focusing the field and retyping the displayed "49" silently rewrites 4999 -> 4900. Overflow path also real: an 8-digit entry like 99999999 -> *100 wraps Int (9,999,999,900 mod 2^32) into garbage that is sent as-is. Two mitigating notes verified: the field uses KeyboardType.Number (line 444), which suppresses the '.' key on most IMEs (decimal entry then arrives via paste), and the backend Joi price_cents min(0) rejects negative wraps — neither prevents the display truncation or the paste/decimal inflation.
fix: Render `"%.2f".format(Locale.US, form.priceCents / 100.0)` (or a money field), parse decimal-aware (digits + one separator -> BigDecimal.movePointRight(2), coerceIn(0, cap)), switch to KeyboardType.Decimal.
Derive the end label in the start's zone: parse slot.start/end as OffsetDateTime and shift end atZoneSameInstant(viewer zone) before formatting.
